contributions.anchor: ⚠ THE DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION — this side closes ONLY on the CUMULATIVE column: Column B 'Year-to-Date Total' contributions (23,469.07) on the p2 Summary Page line 1, which is also the figure printed as 'Total Contributions Received (Sum of subtotals from all Schedule A pages)' on all four Schedule A pages. It does NOT close on the promoted per-period cell, Column A 'Total this Period' (21,574.00).
contributions.detail: The filer's Schedule A here is CYCLE-CUMULATIVE, not period-scoped: p3 is a re-fax of the very sheet he filed in June (its 17 rows, its printed page subtotal 1,895.00, and the June grand total struck through and rewritten as 23,469.07), and pp4-6 continue the same running ledger. Page-subtotal gate, page by page: p3's 17 rows sum to 1,895.00 = its printed 'Subtotal for this page' 1895.00; p4's 17 rows sum to 1,164.07 = its printed subtotal 1164.07; p5's 17 rows sum to 8,685.00 = its printed subtotal 8685.00; p6's 10 rows sum to 11,725.00 = its printed subtotal 11,725.00. All four subtotals sum to 1,895.00 + 1,164.07 + 8,685.00 + 11,725.00 = 23,469.07 EXACTLY = the schedule's own printed grand total = Column B YTD = the cover's line 5 'Subtotal'. So the 61 transcribed rows reconcile to the cent against the CUMULATIVE figure. NOT DONE, and worth stating: no cover was differenced against another filing to synthesize anything. One filer-arithmetic observation, traced and retained verbatim, NOT adjudicated: within this document the rows dated after the June report (pp4-6) sum to 21,574.07 while the filer wrote 21,574.00 in Column A — a 7-cent understatement in HIS per-period cell, which is also why line 3 (1,178.33) + line 4 (21,574.00) = 22,752.33 does not equal his own line 5 (23,469.07); line 5 is the YTD figure carried across. Nothing was nudged; the anchor used is the printed figure the rows actually match.

expenditures.anchor: ⚠ THE SAME DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION — Column B 'Year-to-Date Total' expenditures (23,316.52) on the p2 Summary Page line 2, which is also the figure printed as 'Total Expenditures Received (Sum of subtotals from all Schedule B pages)' on all three Schedule B pages (on p7 and p8 written over a struck earlier figure). It does NOT close on Column A 'Total this Period' (22,599.85).
expenditures.detail: Schedule B is cumulative on the same pattern: p7 is a re-fax of the June Schedule B sheet (same 3 rows, same printed subtotal 716.67, grand total struck and rewritten to 23,316.52), pp8-9 continue it. Page-subtotal gate: p7's 3 counted rows sum to 519.48 + 166.23 + 30.96 = 716.67 = its printed subtotal (its 4th written row is STRUCK THROUGH — see the row note and the frame proof — and is correctly excluded by that very subtotal); p8's 17 rows sum to 12,865.74 = its printed subtotal 12,865.74; p9's 6 rows sum to 9,734.11 = its printed subtotal 9,734.11. Total 716.67 + 12,865.74 + 9,734.11 = 23,316.52 EXACTLY = the printed grand total = Column B YTD = the cover's line 2 Column B. The filer's per-period Column A (22,599.85) is exactly 23,316.52 - 716.67, i.e. his own cumulative minus the June page, but that arithmetic was NOT used to gate anything here; the rows are reconciled against the printed cumulative figure they match.

itemized.in_kind_convention: not applicable — neither schedule prints an in-kind column, no row is annotated in-kind, and the cover has no separate in-kind line. Both conventions were tested (monetary-only and monetary-plus-in-kind) and are identical on this document: 23,469.07 / 23,316.52 either way. NOTE what IS annotated: three contribution rows and four expenditure rows carry the filer's own '(Loan)' notation (candidate loans in, and vendor payments he marks as made from that loan, with 'Lane' written above the parenthesis). Loans are transcribed exactly as the filer entered them, inside the schedule totals, because that is where he put them and the printed subtotals prove it — they are NOT in-kind and were not reclassified.
itemized.escalation_note: 19 tight crops at 900-1600 dpi. FOURTEEN were the mandatory geometry proof (first + last transcribed row on each of the seven schedule pages). FIVE were genuine legibility escalations: (a) p7's struck 4th row, cropped at pct:82.5,28.06,12.0,3.96@p7, rendered '85.00' with a heavy wavy strike drawn through the whole row — proving the strike is on the page and not a fax artifact, and that the page's own 716.67 subtotal excludes it; (b) p7 row 3's date cell at 1600 dpi rendered an OVERWRITTEN cell (a hatched leading loop, then a compressed middle glyph) that cannot be resolved to one date — recorded BLANK with needs_review=1; (c) p7 row 2's date cell at 1600 dpi rendered a clean '6-15-10', the control that proves (b) is a property of that cell and not of the crop; (d) p3 row 14's date cell at 1400 dpi rendered '6' followed by '9-15-10' — two tokens in one cell; (e) p3 row 16's date cell at 1400 dpi rendered '6' followed by '7-15-10'. No escalation touched an amount: every amount was legible at 200 dpi full page and both sides close to the cent.

itemized.notes:
PAGE-FACE CANDIDATE: 'J. Lane Henderson', Democrat, Office Seeking 'County Commissioner' (NO SEAT LETTER PRINTED) - index.csv names NO candidate for this row and takes 'County Commission Seat A' from the channel's directory path; the seat is not inferred here. Filing 2 of THREE this filer made in the 2010 cycle. 9 pages, each classified from its own printed header: p1 cover ('Seven days preceding the General Election' checked; signature dated 10-22-10; clerk stamp 'OCT 26 AM 10:26'), p2 SUMMARY PAGE, pp3-6 Schedule A, pp7-9 Schedule B. Entirely handwritten, entirely a FAX ('SENT BY: JMART; 8017989770; OCT-26-10 10:08-10:11AM; PAGE n/9'), with a vertical fax artifact line down every sheet and page-specific skew from -0.4 to +1.3 deg.

THE STRUCTURAL FINDING, and the reason both sides are 'cumulative-exact': THIS FILER RE-FILES HIS ENTIRE CYCLE LEDGER EACH PERIOD. p3 and p7 are literal re-faxes of the Schedule A and Schedule B sheets he filed on 6/15 - same rows, same page subtotals (1,895.00 and 716.67) - with only the grand-total line struck through and rewritten (1895.00 -> 23,469.07; 716.67 -> 23,316.52). The itemized rows therefore reconcile to the cent against the CUMULATIVE column (Column B), not against the promoted per-period Column A. That is the documented exception, not the norm, and it is stated loudly in both recon blocks. Downstream consequence worth flagging to the coordinator: rows 1-17 of contributions and rows 1-3 of expenditures on THIS record are the same events as the ones on record b2b16869 (the 6/15 filing), because the county published both sheets; they are one ledger re-served, not two sets of gifts. Any candidate-cycle total must NOT add this filing's rows to that one.

THE COVER CHAIN HOLDS, and was checked without being used as a gate: line 3 'Balance at Beginning of Reporting Period' prints 1,178.33, exactly the 6/15 report's printed line 7 close. TWO filer-arithmetic facts are retained verbatim and NOT adjudicated: (1) the filer's own Column A contributions (21,574.00) is 7 cents short of what his new rows actually sum to (21,574.07) - the odd cents come from Blair Hamilton's 29.07 - and (2) his line 5 'Subtotal' prints 23,469.07 (the YTD figure) where line 3 + line 4 would give 22,752.33. Nothing was recomputed or nudged; line 7 (869.22) follows from his line 5 as he wrote it.

FOUR date cells on p3 and one on p7 were AMENDED on this copy and are recorded verbatim-or-blank with needs_review=1 (see the row notes) - a real property of a re-faxed sheet the filer edited by hand before re-sending. PRIVACY: the county published this filing UNREDACTED - donor street addresses are legible on pp3-6 - and none was carried into this record, not even into a note; city and state only.
